study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To quantify individual neuroanatomical heterogeneity in OCD by integrating a normative modeling step (voxel-wise GMV deviations) with non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to discover latent disease factors, relate them to clinical variables, reconcile subject- and group-level findings, and explore subtype structure.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Pearson correlations between factor compositions and clinical measures (Y-BOCS total, age of onset, illness duration); two-sample t-tests for sex differences in factor weights; linear regression mapping group-level unthresholded T-map from disease factors (age, sex, TIV as covariates in group analysis); affinity propagation clustering on factor compositions to identify subtypes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Four robust latent disease factors captured individual heterogeneity in OCD; factor compositions related to symptom severity, onset age, duration, and sex; group-level case–control differences could be quantitatively derived from these factors; two subtypes showed opposite GMV patterns versus controls.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Identified 4 disease factors (2 positive, 2 negative). LOOCV inference of factor compositions showed strong correlations with true weights (R^2: PW1 0.862, PW2 0.903, NW1 0.735, NW2 0.806; all permutation P<0.001). Group-level unthresholded T-map was predicted from factors (R^2=0.700, P<0.001). Clustering yielded 2 subtypes (n=35, n=63); subtype 1 had higher positive-factor weights and lower negative-factor weights than subtype 2 (e.g., PW1 t=6.153, d=1.297; PW2 t=5.597, d=1.180; NW1 t=-3.716, d=-0.783; NW2 t=-7.494, d=-1.580; all FDR<0.001). Subtype 1 showed increased GMV and subtype 2 decreased GMV relative to HCs (SPM12, FDR<0.05, cluster size>100 voxels).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Proposed automatic K selection via stability across 100 NMF runs with Hungarian matching; separated positive/negative deviations prior to NMF; reconciled subject- and group-level findings by regressing group T-map on factors; framework generalizes to infer factor compositions for unseen patients via LOOCV.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Modest sample size; need an independent dataset for validation; only first-episode drug-naive patients included (limits heterogeneity); alcohol and tobacco not controlled; obsessive dimensions not recorded, preventing analysis of factor–symptom-dimension associations.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Single-site 3T GE Discovery MR750 acquisition; all participants Han Chinese and right-handed; CAT12 VBM preprocessing with 1.5 mm isotropic resampling and 6-mm smoothing; group analyses controlled age, sex, TIV; data availability on request; published by Oxford University Press in Cerebral Cortex (Open Access).
